newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-SAMPRAS MARCHES ON, TEARFUL CAPRIATI EXITS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS MARCHES ON, TEARFUL CAPRIATI EXITS.

text.p: World number one Pete Sampras and Swiss teenager Martina Hingis marched into the second round of the Australian Open tennis tournament on Tuesday but former prodigy Jennifer Capriati broke down in tears after an unexpected defeat.
Sampras, top seed and hot favourite for the men's title, stream-rollered Romanian qualifier Dinu Pescariu 6-2 6-4 6-2.

The 16-year-old Hingis, with a multi-million-dollar sportswear endorsement deal newly under her belt, picked up a warning for racket abuse before beating German veteran Barbara Rittner 6-1 7-5 on Centre Court.

But the real drama came off court in the media room where Capriati, whom Hingis replaced as the sport's teenaged darling, broke down in tears after being ousted in the first round of her Australian Open comeback.

Four years after her last appearance in Melbourne, when she reached the quarter-finals at the age of 16, Capriati was beaten 6-2 3-6 6-4 by fellow American Jolene Watanabe in a performance which left a crowd of fans disappointed.
After reaching the final of a Sydney warm-up tournament on Saturday, Capriati had been expected to enjoy a straightforward passage to the second round.

But Watanabe, a 28-year-old who had never previously advanced beyond the first round of the Australian Grand Slam event, was able to sit out the match on the baseline and watch Capriati throw it away.
"I was pretty disappointed. I didn't think I was playing nearly as well as last week," Capriati told a news conference.

Asked how she felt about the warm public support she has enjoyed since returning to tennis, Capriati started to reply: "Just being out there and hearing the crowd..." but then burst into tears and was escorted away sobbing heavily.
Czechoslovak-born Hingis was warned by the umpire for throwing her racket into the net after a service break against her in the second set led to a string of errors.
Even if Hingis fails to deny top seed Steffi Graf a fifth Australian Open crown, her financial future is secure.
An Italian sportswear firm on Tuesday announced a five-year sponsorship deal which will give Hingis at least $7.5 million and up to $12 million if she ousts Graf from the top spot.
Men's 11th seed and former champion Jim Courier survived a first-round scare against Dutchman Sjeng Schalken, beating him 8-6 in the fifth set of a marathon tussle.
Like Sampras and German Boris Becker after their first-round ties, Courier complained that the balls being used in the tournament were too soft.
But tournament director Paul McNamee said the balls were no different from those used last year.
On a sweltering but blustery second day, world number three Arantxa Sanchez Vicario began her campaign with a 6-4 6-4 win against Italian Gloria Pizzichini.
The Spanish baseliner, seeded two in the absence of injured American Monica Seles, has never lost before the quarter-finals in six previous visits to Melbourne but she has yet to lift the title.

In the men's singles, three lower seeds -- number eight Wayne Ferreira of South Africa, Chilean Marcelo Rios at number nine and Spanish 16th seed Alberto Berasategui -- all advanced without dropping a set.
But Dutchman Jan Siemerink, seeded 13, fell by the wayside, losing in five sets to Norway's Christian Ruud.
